reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The slip length b+ = 0.3 is an input borrowed from low-Reynolds-number DNS; compliant-coating drag reduction has never been demonstrated reproducibly at ship Reynolds numbers, and soft layers near U/c_t ~ 0.7 risk hydroelastic waves that add drag, so my best estimate for clean-surface wall shear is 0 %. The soft fibre layer may slightly ease macrofouling release, about 0.3 % of time-averaged friction.
key_assumption_issues: Effective slip length b+ = 0.3 assumed, not computed from the layer properties
Equivalent laminar gap h+ = 28 is a free modelling choice of the Couette surrogate
Steady model cannot represent the fluid-structure interaction that is the mechanism
killer_risks: No drag reduction or even drag increase from hydroelastic instabilities at ship speed
Slime covering the surface decouples the wall motion from the flow
Fibre inclination cannot be controlled reliably on a hull in dock

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: An oil-free bottle-brush matrix leaches much less than an oil-containing coating, but the design's advantage partly comes from being twice as thick, and against oil-free commercial silicones it would be small; about 60 % less leaching is plausible. Keeping the layer soft preserves easier hard-fouling release over the interval, worth under 1 % of time-averaged friction.
key_assumption_issues: Baseline assumes an oil-containing coating; many foul-release coatings are oil-free
Design is 300 um thick against 150 um, which halves its flux in this model
Same diffusivity for sol and oil; pseudo-steady model of a depleting reservoir
killer_risks: Low tear energy of bottle-brush elastomers (10-50 J/m^2): cuts and tears under fenders
Cost of bottle-brush macromers at hull-coating volumes
Lower initial release performance without surface oil

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: Tiling does limit load spreading, but the (a/(a+l))^2 correction is a rough area estimate and viscoelastic barnacle adhesion and embedding on ultra-soft beds remain, so about 60 % lower release stress is realistic, slightly better than the continuous skin. Damage containment helps durability; the objective gain stays about 1.5 % because slime is unaffected.
key_assumption_issues: Load-spreading correction (a/(a+l))^2 is an estimate, not a solved plate-on-foundation problem
Elastic Kendall balance with w = 0.05 J/m^2
Gap material behaviour under contact not modelled
killer_risks: Soft 20 um gaps as weak spots under fenders and as microgrooves for diatom colonisation
Segmentation of a skin at hull scale is slow and costly
Ultra-soft bed gels may be oil-extended and leach
